newsitem.title: FRANCE: Accor sees CDC, Gle de Belgique cut stakes.
newsitem.headline: Accor sees CDC, Gle de Belgique cut stakes.

text.p: France's Accor expects most of its core shareholders to stick to their holdings but the stakes held by state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations and Societe Generale de Belgique could diminish, founders Paul Dubrule and Gerard Pelisson said on Monday.
The two men, interviewed in afternoon daily Le Monde, said that there was a "question mark" over the holdings of the French state bank and the Belgian group.

"The Caisse des Depots -- which has 9.3 percent of the capital and 11.57 percent of the voting rights -- will continue to cut its holding. But it's not a problem, there have been a lot of shareholders in the history of the group," they said.
"The only thing we want is that the market is not upset and that if the Caisse des Depots is going to cut its stake by three or four percent that this will happen off-market," they said.

"Concerning Generale de Belgique, we will speak with them in the coming months. Whether they cut their stake or get rid of it, any significant move will be done in consultation with us. It's in their interest and in ours," the two men said.
"In the future, our shareholders will above all be pension funds, that's where the money is," they said. "Capitalism a la francaise, via cross-shareholdings, will not last," they added.
